_note: Round 23. Closes the remaining 9 of round 21's original 34-country e-GDDS list: the 7 countries round 21 bundled into a single 'not checked this round' dropped entry (Andorra, Albania, Micronesia, Montenegro, Palau, San Marino, Kosovo) plus 2 more (Guyana, Serbia) that round 21 miscounted and never listed at all -- found only because round 22's count-correction pass (25/34 wired, 9 remained, not 7) caught the discrepancy. Method: the IMF's own DSBB e-GDDS country-category page (dsbb.imf.org/e-gdds/country/<ISO3>/category), rendered in Chrome, carries a hidden global country-to-NSDP-URL link list (found via javascript_tool querying all outbound <a> tags -- a plain page-text read only shows the active country's own category rows, not this list) that gave a registered NSDP URL for every one of these 9 countries in one page load, replacing the country-by-country press-release search round 22 used. 7 of the 9 registered destinations were live, self-declared pages (each on the country's own domain) and graded A. The other 2 (Andorra, Micronesia) have registered destinations that are unreadable for different reasons (a JS-shell SPA with no content region; an expired TLS certificate) -- both wired instead as REGISTER-tier edges off the IMF's own press release for that country, per PLAYBOOK-CORPUS.md rule 19 (a document published by the TARGET's own publisher recording the relationship is REGISTER, not THIRD-PARTY, and grades on the same A/B/C rules as any other tier -- both grade A here because both press releases were read in full and quoted verbatim). Two recurring findings, both character-level: the shared NSDP page template has an unsubstituted-placeholder bug ('...in which Country participates', literally, on San Marino/Montenegro/Albania/Serbia's own copies -- confirmed present on 4 of the 7 self-declared pages in this batch, so this is a platform-wide template defect, not a per-country typo); Serbia's page additionally bakes a Unicode replacement character (U+FFFD) into the apostrophe position in its raw HTML, and San Marino's page uses a plain ASCII apostrophe where every other page in this batch uses the U+2019 typographic one. Every quote below was cut to avoid the specific defect(s) present on its own page rather than silently 'fixed', and every apostrophe was verified by code point before transcription. Two of the nine country codes (AD, SM) had no existing corpus node and were missing COUNTRY_FAMILY/COUNTRY_LABEL (palette.ts) and CONTINENT_OF (regions.ts) entries -- both added this round (XEU family, Europe continent, alongside LI/CH's non-EU-European-microstate precedent). The other 7 (AL, FM, ME, PW, RS, XK, GY) already had live nodes elsewhere in the corpus and needed no classification changes. No id or evidence-URL collision against the whole corpus for any of the 9 new nodes or URLs (checked before writing). This closes the e-GDDS wiring todo: all 34 of round 21's original list are now wired (25 self-declared/register from round 21 itself, 4 from round 22's group-1, 9 from this round -- 7 self-declared, 2 register).
